newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber futures end steady in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber futures end steady in thin trade.

text.p: Rubber futures closed steady to easier on Monday in slow, listless trade with most players still nursing a holiday hangover while the short session in Japan weighed on the market, dealers said.
"There's no action at all. People's minds are not yet on the market. Interest should slowly return tomorrow when Japan is open the entire day," a local rubber trader said.

"It was a very thin market because Japan was only open for the first two sessions," another trader said. Tokyo's benchmark June contract fell 1.2 yen to finish at 148.7 while Kobe's June contract slipped one yen to end at 148.9 yen.
Volume was sparse. The most active month was the RSS3 February contract with about 600 tonnes traded against 2,635 tonnes traded last Friday for the same month, dealers said.
At around 0945 GMT, February RSS3 was seen at 123.00-125.00 U.S. cents a kg from the previous 125.00 cents.
April RSS1 was seen at 180.50-182.50 Singapore cents (US$1.29-$1.30) a kg from the previous 181.50 cents.
April TSR20 was seen at 172.00-174.00 Singapore cents (US$1.22-$1.24) a kg from 172.75 cents.
